New Aerospace Technologies 2021 by Alexander V. Frolov, an Russian scientist associated with Faraday Lab Ltd. 

#ufotwitter #ufo

Focuses on unconventional, non-traditional propulsion methods for aerospace applications. It emphasizes active (non-reactive or reactionless) propulsion systems that avoid ejecting mass (unlike rockets or standard jets) to generate thrust or motion. Ideas draw from experimental physics, historical experiments, and the author's theories, often involving electromagnetism, aether concepts, time manipulation, and gravity-like effects.

Key propulsion concepts covered include:

Active/Non-Reactive Propulsion Principles — Core theme: Creating force/motion without expelling reactive mass. This enables "fuel-less" or propellantless drives for vehicles, drones, satellites, or spacecraft.

Electric and Electrokinetic Thrusters — Methods using electric fields, asymmetrical capacitors (e.g., inspired by Thomas Townsend Brown/Biefeld-Brown effect), gradient dielectrics, or electrokinetic effects to produce directional force. Examples include Frolov's own capacitor designs as electric drives and active force nanomaterials.

Electrostatic Pressure and Asymmetrical Field Propulsion — Generating net thrust via non-homogeneous electric fields, Lorentz force analogies (e.g., with rotating or piezoelectric elements), or ponderomotive forces.

Inertial and Gyroscopic Drives — Devices exploiting variable-radius gyroscopes, precession, curvilinear motion, or internal inertial-less processes to manipulate momentum or create apparent propulsion (e.g., inertial drives, gyroscope weight compensation).

Magnus Effect and Lorentz Force Analogies — Comparing aerodynamic lift (Magnus) to electromagnetic forces for propulsion in closed or controlled flows.

Antigravity and Gravimagnetic Effects — Techniques to compensate or reduce weight/gravity, including pondemotor effects, thermogravity, shape-induced effects (e.g., Grebennikov's cavity structural device), and gravimagnetic field experiments.

Chronal (Time-Based) Force and Chronodynamics — Advanced/speculative concept: Using "chronal force" to alter time rate (speed of processes) in a localized space via energy density gradients or aether pressure. This creates propulsion as a byproduct of time manipulation (e.g., waves of "time density" per Kozyrev, 4-D resonances, chronal motive power). Ties into teleportation concepts and spacetime engineering.

Other Experimental/Historical Approaches — Coverage of devices like Korovin's aether apparatus, Ignatiev's ponderolet, Brown's effect variants, longitudinal waves, de Broglie matter waves, and internal force movement.
